title: Paired differences in sales before and after training
scenario_markdown: Eight randomly sampled sales reps have before sales (units/week) 40, 42, 45, 39, 50, 48, 43, 46 and corresponding after sales 42, 46, 48, 44, 51, 52, 45, 49. Each position is the same rep. Define d=after-before. At alpha=0.05, test H0: mean difference=0 against H1: mean difference>0. Without an untreated randomized control group, this comparison alone does not establish training causation.
assumptions: Differences from distinct reps are independent and approximately normally distributed for the small-sample t method.
The alternative is right-sided for d=after-before, specified before seeing results.
Pairing is by rep; the two measurement arrays are not independent samples.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is the mean after-minus-before difference in units per week? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: The stated difference is after minus before.
24 is the sum of eight differences; divide by eight.

stages.explanation_markdown: Differences are 2,4,3,5,1,4,2,3. Their sum is 24, so mean difference is 3. Excel: subtract before from after in a helper column and use `=AVERAGE(C2:C9)`.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is the paired t statistic for the zero-difference null? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: Divide SD by sqrt(8) to get the standard error of the mean difference.
The positive mean difference gives a positive statistic.

stages.explanation_markdown: Squared deviations of differences from 3 sum to 12; $s_d^2=12/7$. Thus $t=3/\sqrt{(12/7)/8}=\sqrt{42}=6.4807$, df=7. Excel: `=AVERAGE(C2:C9)/(STDEV.S(C2:C9)/SQRT(COUNT(C2:C9)))`.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is the p-value for the stated right-sided alternative? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: Use the right tail because H1 specifies a positive mean difference.
Alpha is not the observed p-value.

stages.explanation_markdown: Use the signed t statistic in `=T.DIST.RT(t,7)`. Here the observed sign agrees with H1, so the one-tail probability equals half the two-sided p-value. This halving shortcut would be wrong for a right-sided alternative with a negative observed t.

options.text_markdown: Reject the zero-difference null; mean after sales are higher under the model, but the before/after design alone does not prove training caused the increase.
Treat the 16 measurements as independent observations with df=14.
options.hint_markdown: There are eight independent differences, giving df=7.

options.text_markdown: The small p-value proves all reps improve and the training is the sole cause.
options.hint_markdown: A population mean comparison neither guarantees every individual outcome nor eliminates time confounding.

stages.explanation_markdown: The right-sided p-value is below 0.05. Pairing removes between-person levels from the difference, while temporal changes and other causes can still confound attribution.
